quote: For by instinct, we human beings only live in half the world.
content: Positive testing is not uniformly bad, and Fable correctly demands attention to the candidate rules and available tests. That does not imply it is optimal in this task or that a default strategy cannot be a predictable source of error under identifiable conditions. Klayman & Ha (1987) motivates checking diagnosticity; a framing change that helps subjects consider excluded cases is a possible correction to the observed failure, not evidence that no failure existed.

quote: but phlogiston theory could just as well have explained the flame not going out
content: A specified finite-capacity phlogiston model does constrain how long combustion can continue, so the unrestricted historical assertion needs correction. That does not establish Fable's repeated account of how Priestley discovered oxygen; see Astra's source check. The experiment's evidential value depends on what this version of the theory predicted before the observation, not on which retrospective label either annotator prefers.

quote: I replied that non-superconductivity and non-ferromagnetism were also examples of emergence, which was the problem.
content: Calling a phenomenon chemical or emergent can help locate a field of inquiry without explaining which outcome will occur. A collective model with a critical temperature supplies much more information than merely saying that both phases are emergent. Fable is right that the category is not empty; the essay is right that citing membership in it does not substitute for the model.
